newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Virgin boss prepares for round-world balloon flight.
newsitem.headline: Virgin boss prepares for round-world balloon flight.

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson started preparing in the Moroccan city of Marrakesh on Saturday for his second attempt to be the first to fly around the world by balloon.
Branson arrived in his private jet at Marrakesh civil airport on Friday night with one of his two co-pilots.
"We started on Saturday the first training and we plan a professional set-up tomorrow for reporters and photographers," a spokeswoman said.
Branson checked out the navigation and control instruments in the balloon's capsule at Marrakesh military airport. Reporters were barred from the airfield and Branson was not available for comment.
Branson said on Friday he planned to return to Britain on Monday but if the weather was promising he might stay to start the attempt next week.
"But it will definitely be before the end of January, depending on the weather," he said.
Branson and co-pilots Per Linstrand, who built the prototype balloon, and hang-gliding champion Rory McCarthy, aim to be first to fly by balloon round the world and expect to do it in about 18 days.

The British entrepreneur, who has brushed with death twice on record-breaking balloon flights, faces a race from American balloonist Steve Fosset and a two-man team planning a launch from Switzerland.
Last January Branson had to abandon an attempt from Marrakesh because of the weather. The 45-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies described his expedition at the time as a "mad adventure".
